prompt.context: Our client Apogee Bank is a regional bank with 700 branches in the US Midwest. It has seen a declining trend in revenues in the past 2 years. Blake Moran, the CEO of Apogee Bank, hired you to identify the reasons for falling revenues and recommend ways to grow revenues. Apogee Bank offers checking and savings accounts, as well as personal, mortgage and auto loans. On the checking and savings accounts, Apogee Bank makes money from service charges and account maintenance fees, whereas it earns interest on loans. Apogee Bank provides services through both brick-and-mortar branches and online applications.
prompt.question: What are the reasons for Apogee Bank's falling revenues over the past 2 years, and how should the bank grow revenues going forward?

clarifying_info.q: What other products or services does Apogee Bank offer?
clarifying_info.a: The information provided covers the full product lineup. No additional products are relevant for this case.

clarifying_info.q: Are costs or profitability also a concern?
clarifying_info.a: The focus of this engagement is on revenues. Please direct your analysis accordingly.

clarifying_info.q: Is this decline happening across all products?
clarifying_info.a: Please look at the exhibit when it is provided to analyze product-level trends.

exhibits.title: Average Revenue Per Account (ARPA) by Product
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing Total Revenue (in millions) on the left axis and Average Revenue Per Account (ARPA) on the right axis, tracked from 2016 to 2020, broken out by three product lines: Checking/Savings Accounts, Loans, and Other Products. A footnote states that the number of accounts per customer and the mix and volume of transactions within each account type have remained almost the same across all products in the last 5 years.

data.footnote: # Accounts per customer and mix/volume of transactions within each account type have remained almost the same across all products in the last 5 years

exhibits.title: Summary of email survey conducted on churning customers
exhibits.shows: Two charts: (1) Where survey respondents switched to, showing counts for Digital Banks (780), National Banks (478), Competitor Regional Banks (195), Other Institutions (78), and an unlabeled segment (29). (2) A horizontal bar chart of reasons for switching, listing: High interest rates on deposits, Digital platforms/Online capabilities, Customer Service, Low fees, Access to wealth management products, Advice on financial health, Access to a banker — each with an approximate percentage bar up to ~70-80%.

exhibits.title: Partner with WizardTech or Buy Finvest Inc.?
exhibits.shows: A side-by-side comparison table of two options for launching investment/wealth management products. WizardTech is a B2B tech company offering white-labelled investment products and services to retail financial services companies. Finvest Inc. is a New Jersey-based FinTech startup offering personal wealth management services. Key financial parameters are listed for each option. A footnote states that Apogee Bank expects Finvest to immediately save 6% on fixed costs and improve contribution margin by 5% if the deal goes through.

data.footnote: Apogee Bank expects Finvest to immediately save 6% on fixed costs and improve contribution margin by 5% if the deal goes through

framework: Change in market dynamics: Competition (new regional banks, better rates from online/national competitors, consolidation), Customer trends (millennials/GenZ shifting to digital/challenger banks, lack of rewards)
Government/Regulatory reasons: caps on reserves limiting lending, additional onboarding paperwork
Revenue decomposition: Revenue = # of Customers x # of Accounts per Customer x ARPA
ARPU/ARPA analysis: If ARPA is flat but total revenue is falling, then the number of accounts (i.e., customers) must be decreasing
Primary diagnosis: Customer churn is the root cause of falling revenues
Growth opportunities — Organic: price adjustments, market expansion (new accounts), market penetration (cross-sell), diversification (new products)
Growth opportunities — Inorganic: acquire fintechs or other banks to gain market share

questions.prompt: Given Exhibit 1, what is the primary reason for Apogee Bank's falling revenues?
questions.guidance: Candidate should decompose Revenue = # Accounts x ARPA. Since the exhibit shows ARPA has remained flat/constant across all product lines while total revenue has fallen, and the footnote confirms that # of accounts per customer and transaction mix have not changed, the conclusion is that the total number of customers (accounts) is declining — i.e., customer churn is the root cause. Strong candidates link ARPU = ARPA x # Accounts per user and note that since accounts per user are constant, the user count itself must be falling.

math.setup: Revenue = # Customers x Accounts per Customer x ARPA. If ARPA is constant and Accounts per Customer is constant (per footnote), then Revenue decline => # Customers declining.
steps: ARPA across all products shown as flat 2016-2020
Footnote: # accounts per customer and transaction mix unchanged
Therefore: falling revenue = falling number of customers
math.answer: Customer churn is the primary driver of declining revenues

questions.prompt: Given Exhibit 2, what are the primary reasons customers are churning, and what should Apogee Bank do next?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that the largest group of churning customers switched to Digital Banks (780), followed by National Banks (478). From the reasons for switching, the top drivers are: high interest rates on deposits, digital platforms/online capabilities, and access to wealth management products and financial advice. The key insight is that Apogee lacks investment/personal finance products offered digitally. Strong candidates consolidate these findings to recommend launching digital wealth management/investment products as the priority next step, then move to evaluating how to do so (Exhibit 3).

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, calculate the payback period for both the WizardTech partnership and the Finvest acquisition. Which option is more financially attractive?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate total yearly cost, total yearly revenue, yearly incremental profit, and payback period for each option. Should recognize and apply the cost synergies (6% fixed cost savings, 5% contribution margin improvement) from the footnote for Finvest from inception. Strong candidates structure the two calculations separately before comparing.

math.setup: Partner WizardTech: Total Yearly Cost = Setup Cost amortized or Total Fixed + Variable; Total Revenue = Unit Revenue x Users. Buy Finvest: Apply synergies to fixed cost and contribution margin from day one.
steps: Finvest — Unit variable cost (with 5% CM improvement): $150,000 x (1 - 6%) = $141,000 fixed cost; contribution margin $4 x (1 + 5%) = $4 x 1.05... (per Exhibit: contribution margin $4, improved by 5% = $4.20, but calc uses $3.8 as shown)
Finvest — Per user economics: ARPU = $8 (implied from exhibit data: $800,000/100,000); variable cost per user = $4 x (1-5%) = $3.8
math.answer: WizardTech payback: ~7.5 years. Finvest acquisition payback: ~6.2 years. Finvest is more financially attractive on a payback basis.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some other pros and cons of acquiring Finvest Inc. over partnering with WizardTech?

categories.name: Pros of Acquiring Finvest
ideas: Access to new resources and competencies — additional customers, employees, assets, and IP
Reduced entry barriers to launching wealth management services
Increased bottom-line profitability once integration is complete
Increased market power; better positioned to compete against digital banks and national banks
Potential immediate and long-term tax advantages

categories.name: Cons of Acquiring Finvest
ideas: High initial capital required for the acquisition ($5M buy price)
Risk of losing key employees and customers if integration is mismanaged
Risk of financial detriment if Finvest does not have enough value to justify the investment
Longer implementation time and distraction from day-to-day operations
Regulatory constraints that may limit or delay the acquisition

recommendation: Acquire Finvest Inc. at $5M — payback period of approximately 6.2 years is shorter than the WizardTech partnership (~7.5 years)
Extend Finvest's investment and personal wealth management product offerings to all existing Apogee Bank customers to address the primary churn driver (lack of digital investment products)
risks: The acquisition may not deliver expected benefits if integration is mismanaged or prolonged
Apogee Bank has no prior experience selling wealth management products, which may create marketing and onboarding challenges
Finvest's intent to sell and confidence in maintaining its current financials are not fully known
Customer adoption of new investment products offered through Apogee may be slow
next_steps: Ensure sufficient liquid funds are available to fund the $5M acquisition
Develop a phased integration strategy to merge with Finvest and roll out investment products
Explore ways to realize additional synergies post-acquisition beyond the 6% cost and 5% margin improvements
Monitor customer adoption rates and adjust go-to-market strategy for new wealth management offerings
